Artificial intelligence simulation study of Therapeutic Plasma Exchange (TPE) using an 8- State Markov State-Transition Model integrated within a Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo Framework.
desc: [Research square] Introduction Sepsis-induced organ dysfunction remains a leading cause of mortality in critical care. While recent evidence suggests that Therapeutic Plasma Exchange (TPE) may improve outcomes, significant heterogeneity among septic patient populations in prior trials might have contributed to mixed responses and thus fueled clinical skepticism. To address this challenge and to model TPE effectiveness across varying levels of sepsis severity, we utilized a time-dependent, 8-state transition Markov model integrated with a Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) framework. Methods An AI-generated "digital twin" cohort (N = 10,000) was randomized 1:1 to standard care (SC) or adjuvant TPE groups. Transition probabilities were parameterized using a pooled relative risk (RR) of 0.58, derived from five recent meta-analyses. The model incorporated specific hazard multipliers for acute kidney injury (AKI; 1.5x), thrombocytopenia (1.3x), and high-dose vasopressor requirements (1.25x). Patient flow was simulated through eight clinically defined health states over a 28-day horizon. Outcomes included 28-day survival, absolute risk reduction (ARR), and number needed to treat (NNT) stratified by Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score quartiles (8, 12, 16, and 20). Bayesian methods were employed to determine survival probabilities and hazard ratios (HR) with 95% credible intervals (CrI). Results Across the modelled full 10,000-patient cohort, TPE increased 28 day survival compared to standard care (67.3% vs. 44.7%). The survival benefit was modest in the group with the lowest degree of organ failure (SOFA 8) (TPE 87.6% vs. SC 78.4%; ARR 9.2%; NNT 11). However, this benefit was more pronounced in cases of higher burden of organ failure, particularly within the SOFA 20 cohort (TPE 48.8% vs. SC 12.8%; ARR 36%; NNT 3) and in cases with AKI + thrombocytopenia + higher doses of vasopressors (ARR 36%; NNT 3). For SOFA 20 patients, TPE was associated with a 38% reduction in the hazard of death (HR 0.62; 95% CrI 0.54-0.71). Conclusion These simulation results suggests that the efficacy of TPE might be dependent on baseline illness severity. While the clinical impact is more limited in moderate sepsis (SOFA 8), TPE appears to offer a profound survival advantage and high therapeutic yield for patients with multi-organ failure.

title: Multilingual Artificial Datasets for AI-Driven Cardiology: the CliTe and ParaCliTe corpora
desc: Background and Aims. Comparable, multilingual, validated cardiology corpora are critical to advance trustworthy natural language processing (NLP) models for cardiology but such resources are scarce due to privacy concerns. This study aimed to cover this gap by presenting suitable artificial corpus creation guidelines and by releasing 3 multilanguage corpora. Methods. Following purpose-specific publicly-available corpus construction guidelines, cardiologists from 7 European hospitals generated artificial clinical records in Czech, Dutch, English, Italian, Romanian, Spanish and Swedish, ensuring clinical diversity and sex balance, resulting in the CliTe corpus. A CliTe subset underwent a multi-stage manual translation into the other 6 languages, resulting in the parallel ParaCliTe corpus, while the remaining reports were automatically translated, constituting ParaCliTe Silver. Results. CliTe is a collection of 699 artificial cardiology reports, mostly outpatient notes (340 documents), discharge reports (263), and inpatient notes (89), describing fictional patients with ischaemic heart disease (199 patients), heart failure (188), and valvular disease (79), among others. ParaCliTe contains reports from 94 fictitious patients, each available in seven languages with sentence-level alignment, resulting in 658 documents. The corpus mainly comprises discharge reports (322 documents), and outpatient (196) and inpatient (140) notes, describing patients with heart failure (399 documents), ischaemic heart disease (287), and valvular disease (238). Empirical results illustrate the utility of ParaCliTe and highlight the limitations of state-of-the-art NLP models adapted to the cardiology domain. Conclusions. The creation of multilingual, equitable and realistic corpora of artificial patients capable of strengthening NLP performance for cardiology is feasible when supported by detailed guidelines.

title: Rapid generation of antibody conformational ensembles using machine learning
desc: We introduce Cadense, a generative framework for antibody ensemble prediction that produces diverse Fv structures from sequence, informed by conformational dynamics. While a valuable resource, static structure prediction provides only a single snapshot of dynamic proteins, whose motions influence their binding and other properties. This is particularly relevant for antibodies, an important class of molecules for drug discovery, where flexible complementarity determining region (CDR) loops are difficult to model with static approaches. Cadense addresses this gap by generating ensembles that match conformational and biophysical property distributions from molecular dynamics (MD), while reducing the computational burden from days of simulation to seconds of generation. We show Cadense ensembles can recover both apo and holo conformations of the same antibody and serve as effective input to physics-based docking, capturing the conformational flexibility important to properly model antibody antigen interactions. Together, these results establish Cadense as a useful tool for antibody conformational ensemble generation with the promise to enable faster, dynamics-aware antibody design.

title: Foundation Model Artificial Intelligence for Electrocardiogram Detection of Rheumatic Mitral Stenosis.
source: PubMed · medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
desc: [medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences] Rheumatic mitral stenosis (RMS) disproportionately affects low-resource settings where echocardiography is limited. We evaluated foundation model (FM) feasibility for RMS detection using limited, indirectly labeled ECGs. An ECG-FM was fine-tuned using 804 RMS-positive ECGs per fold and externally validated across clinical and wearable lead configurations. Internal AUROCs were 0.89, 0.87, and 0.87, for 12-Lead, 6-Lead, and 1-Lead respectively. External AUROCs were 0.82, 0.80, and 0.77. Performance remained comparable across demographic subgroups. FM fine-tuning enables RMS detection using limited ICD-derived labels, supporting further evaluation of reduced-lead ECG screening and echocardiography triage in resource-constrained settings.

title: Can Agentic Systems Close the Gap in Radiology with Production AI Tools?
desc: Radiology AI has developed along two paths: specialized models that perform well on narrow tasks but cover few clinical findings, and generalist models that address a broader range of tasks but remain prone to hallucination and inaccurate measurements. Combining the two through agentic systems offers a route towards comprehensive radiology reporting, but published systems are tied to one modality or body part. We describe a radiology agentic framework that standardizes how an orchestrator calls modular tools to produce a structured report, and use it to measure what such a system can do with the tools from FDA-cleared radiology AI devices. Report generation is simulated on a large multi-modality report corpus, with the orchestrator given either a catalog of finding classes consolidated from the cleared devices, each available on the modalities it is cleared for, or an unlimited catalog in which any class can be requested, and planning either from the clinical indication or from the target report. Tool outputs are simulated from the reference report, so the comparison isolates tool availability and orchestration from tool error. With the cleared catalog and the indication alone, the orchestrator recovers under a third of the clinically actionable findings; recovery improves substantially with the unlimited catalog, and further when the plan is written from the target report. Attributing every missed finding to a cause shows that most are classes no cleared device offers for the study's modality, and that a third are classes or tools that were offered and not called. Adding the most frequently missing tools closes most of the gap to the unlimited catalog on held-out reports, whereas a smaller orchestrator with the unlimited catalog gives up the whole gain. Tool availability and effective orchestration are thus complementary constraints on comprehensive AI-assisted radiology reporting.

title: GeneEmbedLLM: Harnessing Large Language Models for Gene Functional Embedding and Association Prediction
desc: Effective and high-quality gene function representations are crucial for bioinformatics tasks. While biological knowledge about genes is inherently textual, encompassing functional descriptions and pathway annotations, current methods often rely on single-source, non-textual data, failing to capture the rich semantic information in multi-source gene annotations. In this paper, we propose GeneEmbedLLM, a Large Language Model (LLM)-powered framework for generating universal, semantically-aware gene embeddings. The proposed approach advances the gene representation learning through multi-source structured text integration from five authoritative databases and attribute-aware attention based on Longformer architecture and contrastive learning. Experimental results on diverse downstream tasks, ranging from molecular interactions and phenotypic dependencies to epigenetic regulation, confirm the validity and effectiveness of our proposed approach, where competitive performance is achieved across all evaluated benchmarks. We further validate the quality of the generated embeddings through comprehensive analyses, including embedding visualizations, intra-pathway similarity assessments, ablation study, and parameter analysis.

title: Deep learning pulmonary vessel segmentation for contrast-enhanced and non-contrast CT images.
desc: [Medical physics] Accurate and comprehensive segmentation of pulmonary vasculature is essential for diagnosing various pulmonary diseases and lung surgical planning. To develop a deep learning model for pulmonary vessels segmentation based on both computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) and non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) data, and to evaluate its performance on a clinical dataset. In this retrospective study, we collected 427 cases of chest CT data from different countries and manufacturers, including 213 CTPA cases and 214 NCCT cases. And we designed a CTPA and NCCT ground truth (GT) generation method producing high-accuracy vessel annotation dataset. Then we developed a 3D U-Net based deep learning method with the Vessel Lumen Structure Optimization Module (VLSOM). We numerically evaluated model using metrics including Centerline Recall (Cl-Recall), Centerline DICE (Cl-DICE), Average Symmetric Surface Distance (ASSD) and 95% Hausdorff Distance (HD95) focusing on the integrity of vascular structures. Finally, the model performance was visually assessed in an independent external dataset. In the numerical evaluation on the internal test dataset with 57 cases, our model achieved Cl-DICE, Cl-Recall and HD95 values of 0.909 (95% CI [0.904, 0.914]), 0.883 (95% CI [0.873, 0.891]) and 1.861 mm (95% CI [1.674 mm, 2.073 mm]) which is superior to the state of the art (SOTA) baseline model nnU-Net v2 of 0.860 (95% CI [0.852, 0.867]), 0.772 (95% CI [0.760, 0.783])and 2.458 mm (95% CI [2.219 mm, 2.708 mm]) (all p < 0.001). In the clinical visual assessments on the 90 sets of external datasets, the average score for accuracy and robustness, branch abundance, computer-aided detection and vascular continuity 4.52 (95% CI [4.42, 4.62]), 4.82 (95% CI [4.76, 4.90]), 4.58 (95% CI [4.46, 4.69]), and 4.85 (95% CI [4.77, 4.92]) respectively with a full score of 5. The proposed pulmonary vessel segmentation algorithm performed well in preserving the connectivity and integrity of the vascular structure on both CTPA and NCCT data with various diseases. A vessel centerline topology-enhanced deep segmentation model enables accurate and automatic pulmonary vessel segmentation in both computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) and non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) images.

title: Beyond Segmentation: Enriching ImageCAS with Coronary Ostia Landmarks, Rooted Centerline Graphs, and Open-Weight Localization Models
desc: Coronary ostia and centerlines are key reference points for automated analysis of coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA), from surgical planning to intraoperative vessel tracking. However, the only public ostium annotations cover 77 non-gated aortic scans, not CCTA, while CAT08 and ASOCA (32 and 40 CCTA scans) mark the ostia only implicitly, as centerline start points. This work enriches ImageCAS, the largest public dataset for coronary artery segmentation, with ostium annotations for its 1000 patients and centerline graphs rooted at these new ostia, making it, to the authors' knowledge, the largest public dataset for ostium localization and the only one with centerlines following the official ImageCAS masks and starting at annotated ostia. Three annotators marked each ostium in the first 500 volumes; in the next 500, the candidates of a model trained on the first batch were corrected (human-in-the-loop). Six 3D localization models, trained on ImageCAS, CAT08 and ASOCA, were benchmarked on 58 held-out volumes (50 ImageCAS, 4 CAT08, 4 ASOCA). SwinUNETR-V2 and nnResUNet localized all ostia without failure (>5 mm error), with median errors of 0.70-0.87 mm. Trained on CAT08 and ASOCA alone, SwinUNETR-V2 fails on 34% of right and 53% of left ostia, whereas adding 250 ImageCAS volumes removes all failures. The centerlines were extracted by a deterministic, quality-controlled minimal-path procedure; on ASOCA, they cover a median of 99.5% of the reference length, with a median per-patient mean distance of 0.22 mm between matched reference points and centerlines. Annotations, centerlines, code, and weights are available at https://hal9000-lab.github.io/.

title: π-SPECFormer: A Mass Spectrometry-based Foundation Model for Decoding the Dark Proteome
desc: In mass-spectrometry-based proteomics, a substantial proportion of acquired spectra remain unidentified, concealing a vast reservoir of biological variations commonly termed the "dark proteome", potentially obscuring sequence mutations, non-canonical peptides and post-translational modifications. Existing deep-learning methods largely rely on supervised training with peptide-spectrum matches (PSMs), limiting their ability to learn from the much larger pool of unannotated spectra. Here we introduce {pi}-SPECFormer, a mass-spectrometry foundation model pre-trained on 291 million spectra through a two-stage framework that combines self-supervised and PSMs-guided representation learning. {pi}-SPECFormer transfers effectively to de novo peptide sequencing, spectrum clustering and modification detection, consistently outperforming task-specific baselines. When applied to proteomic profiles from 103 individuals with lung adenocarcinoma, the model identified nine high-confidence mutated peptides, including six that were absent from the reference databases. {pi}-SPECFormer thus enables unbiased decoding of molecular complexity beyond the boundaries of the canonical proteome.

title: Oculomics in Gastrointestinal Disorders: A narrative review.
desc: [Romanian journal of ophthalmology] We reviewed various ocular biomarkers relevant to gastrointestinal (GI) disorders and examined the potential role of artificial intelligence (AI) in detecting, integrating, and translating these biomarkers into clinical gastroenterology practice. A literature search from PubMed, MEDLINE, Scopus, Google Scholar, and Web of Science from the year 2000 up to February 2026 was conducted. We included published articles on ocular findings in gastrointestinal disorders and/or AI-based analysis of ocular biomarkers with gastrointestinal connections. Results suggested a positive correlation between AI-based ocular biomarkers and GI disorders. After reviewing the literature, we found that the most frequently described ocular biomarkers were retinal vascular caliber and arteriovenous ratio on fundus photography; retinal nerve fibre layer and choroidal changes on optical coherence tomography; and vessel-density changes on optical coherence tomography angiography. The persistent signal came from inflammatory bowel disease and steatotic liver disease. AI may improve image processing, feature extraction, and pattern recognition, but more multicentric studies are needed to establish definitive analogy. This review suggests that ocular biomarkers could provide a simple, non-invasive way to identify and monitor gastrointestinal diseases, especially inflammatory bowel disease and steatotic liver disease. Changes in retinal blood vessels, the retinal nerve fibre layer, the choroid, and OCTA-derived vessel density may reflect the inflammation, metabolic disturbances, and small-vessel changes associated with these conditions. However, these findings should be interpreted with caution because many existing studies included small or selected patient groups, used cross-sectional designs, applied different imaging methods, and did not consistently account for factors such as age, vascular risk, medications, or coexisting eye disease. Artificial intelligence may improve the analysis of complex eye images by identifying subtle patterns. Still, high model performance alone does not prove that these tools are accurate, reliable, or specific enough for clinical use. Future studies should therefore include large, multicentre, prospective populations, standardized imaging and reporting methods, independent external validation, and clinically meaningful outcomes. These steps will help determine whether AI-assisted oculomics can reliably support gastrointestinal screening, disease classifica

title: ICare-DT: a digital twin for continuous forecasting of intensive care patients
desc: Digital twins of intensive care patients should update forecasts from new data and predict treatment responses, but few studies test whether routine records support either. We propose ICare-DT, a Transformer-based twin that updates a latent patient state hourly from new measurements without retraining. We trained it on 140,473 eICU-CRD stays to forecast vital signs crossing their training-set means. On test data, later forecasts beat the twin's own hour-6 forecasts of the same windows in all 12 settings (+0.073 to +0.153 AUROC). On validation data, controls that withheld or swapped the new hours traced the gain to the patient's own measurements. Without refitting, the model kept its gain on a second database (8 of 9 settings, +0.025 to +0.114 AUROC) in a prespecified evaluation of the previously analyzed MIMIC-IV test split. Refitted within MIMIC-IV, a twin state fine-tuned on clinical endpoints gave gradient boosting a significant gain for acute kidney injury (+0.0035 AUROC; hypotension +0.0010, not significant). To test response prediction, we built a benchmark that replaces the treatments in real records with simulated doses and injects responses of known size, visible only at measurement times. Ridge models supervised with injected effects recovered them from real records only through frequently measured variables (heart rate) read at their measurement times. We asked standard learners to predict these effects for a dosing regime no patient had received. No standard learner outperformed predicting zero effect at an out-of-support query. When told how the simulated responses were generated, a separate learner recovered the effects from the same records without seeing their true values (R2 0.30 to 0.40 at one effect size). Routine records support forecasts that improve with each patient's new data, and our benchmark is a testbed for models that learn how responses are generated.

title: ACHC: a novel deep learning model for tomato leaf disease.
desc: [Plant cell reports] The expansion of commercial tomato cultivation creates a pressing need for accurate, automated disease diagnosis to support modern agriculture. To address this, we developed an enhanced AlexNet model integrated with Coordinate and Hybrid Channel-spatial attention (ACHA) for tomato leaf disease recognition. The classical AlexNet was first streamlined to reduce computational overhead, tailored to the characteristics of tomato disease imagery. A coordinate attention module was then inserted after Conv1 and Conv3 to improve spatial localization of lesion areas. Additionally, a hybrid channel-spatial attention module was incorporated after Conv2 and Conv4 to strengthen discriminative feature learning across channels. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves an average test accuracy of 99.62%, outperforming several state-of-the-art deep learning networks such as MobileNetV3 and ResNet50. This work provides an effective and lightweight solution for automated disease monitoring, contributing to more precise and sustainable tomato production systems.

title: MSR-ABC: Complementary Feature Fusion for Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma Classification
desc: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) classification from computed tomography (CT) may benefit from representations that capture different aspects of tumour phenotype. However, simply concatenating reconstruction-derived features, image--text embeddings, and radiomic descriptors may not fully exploit their complementary information. We propose MSR-ABC, a global--local framework integrating MedVAE, MedSigLIP, and radiomics. Spatially matched local image descriptors interact through cross-representation attention, while radiomic auxiliary supervision encourages the pooled local representation to retain quantitative tumour attributes. A gated residual mechanism integrates local information with global summaries. Area-aware pooling and visual and soft-text prompting complete the framework. We evaluate discrimination using a patient-level split of 396 KiTS23 cases and an external cohort of 111 TCGA/TCIA cases, reporting mean AUROC over three training seeds with 95% patient-bootstrap confidence intervals. MSR-ABC achieves mean AUROCs of 0.806 internally and 0.879 externally. Internally, it exceeds global MedVAE--radiomics and three-source concatenation by 3.35 and 3.61 AUROC percentage points, respectively. Removing any source lowers mean AUROC in both cohorts, with the largest decreases following radiomics removal. Individual removal of cross-representation attention, auxiliary supervision, or gated fusion also lowers internal mean AUROC. These findings are consistent with complementary contributions within the integrated architecture and support further investigation of structured representation fusion for non-invasive renal tumour characterisation.

title: Ethical Governance of Artificial Intelligence in Nursing Management: Frameworks, Challenges, and Leadership Imperatives.
desc: [Journal of nursing management] Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in healthcare organizations, influencing workforce management, operational decision-making, quality monitoring, and resource allocation. While AI offers opportunities to improve efficiency and organizational performance, its implementation also introduces significant ethical challenges related to privacy, transparency, accountability, bias, and workforce equity. Nurse leaders occupy a pivotal position in shaping how AI is integrated into healthcare systems and ensuring that technological innovation aligns with professional nursing values. This editorial examines ethical AI governance as a leadership imperative in nursing management, drawing on the American Nurses Association Code of Ethics, World Health Organization guidance, leadership theory, sociotechnical systems theory, and equity-centered scholarship. Key ethical concerns associated with AI-enabled management are explored, including algorithmic bias, workforce surveillance, explainability, and accountability in decision-making. The discussion highlights the responsibility of nurse managers to establish governance structures that protect human dignity, promote justice, and preserve professional judgment. To support this work, the Ethical AI Governance Framework for Nursing Management (EAG-NM) is proposed as a conceptual model integrating ethical foundations, leadership imperatives, sociotechnical dynamics, equity safeguards, and organizational governance. The framework positions nurse leaders as ethical stewards of AI adoption and emphasizes workforce readiness, interdisciplinary oversight, and organizational accountability. As AI continues to transform healthcare operations, nursing leadership must move beyond technology implementation toward intentional governance that ensures AI is deployed in ways that are transparent, equitable, and consistent with the profession's moral commitments.

title: Overview of the ImageCLEFmedical 2026 GANs task: Exploring fingerprint detection, privacy leakage, and synthetic medical image generation
desc: The 2026 ImageCLEFmedical GANs Task Exploring Fingerprint Detection, Privacy Leakage, and Synthetic Medical Image Generation continues to investigate privacy and security concerns around using patient data to generate synthetic medical images, now in its fourth edition. This edition introduces three complementary subtasks: the first extends prior editions by asking participants to detect which real images were used in training a Generative Adversarial Network to produce given synthetic outputs; the second is a novel subtask requiring participants to identify which latent vector produced each synthetic image, probing the faithfulness and reversibility of the latent-to-image mapping; the third asks participants to generate privacy-preserving CT slices, quantifying the trade-off between image fidelity and patient privacy. Ground-truth annotations and benchmark datasets of real and GAN-generated lung CT slices are provided for all subtasks. Evaluation is based on Cohen's Kappa for Subtask 1, matching accuracy for Subtask 2, and a combination of FID and Privacy Preservation Score (PPS) for Subtask 3. Overall, 37 teams registered for the task, with 10 teams submitting runs across subtasks and 6 teams submitting working notes papers. This paper presents an overview of the task setup, datasets, evaluation metrics, and summarises the approaches and results of participating teams.

title: Exploring clinician attitudes towards artificial intelligence-generated discharge summaries.
desc: [Internal medicine journal] We conducted an exploratory mixed-methods study of clinician attitudes and editing behaviours towards artificial intelligence (AI)-generated discharge summaries. Five clinicians reviewed three summaries and indicated what changes they would make and why, answered a questionnaire, engaged in semi-structured interviews and viewed screen mock-ups of additional editing features. All clinicians expressed positive sentiments and saw AI as saving time. Edits were driven by professional pride and etiquette, most of which were not corrections of factual errors but optimisation of structure, coherence, conciseness, reasoning and tone. Tension arose between desire for personalised content versus potential benefits of standardisation. Various novel editing features were seen as expediting summary review.

title: Controllable Molecule Generation via Sparse Representation Editing: An Interpretability-Driven Perspective
desc: Controllable molecule generation is crucial for diverse scientific applications, such as drug discovery and materials design. While large language models (LLMs) show great promise, their dense and entangled representations impede precise control over the generation of molecules with bespoke substructures or properties. To address this, we propose Sparse Representation Editing (SpaRE), an interpretability-driven framework for fine-grained and precise control in LLM-based molecule generation. The crux of SpaRE is to learn an overcomplete sparse feature space that disentangles LLM representations into a compact set of latent features corresponding to chemically meaningful concepts. Within this space, we can directly manipulate these concept-aligned latent features to achieve (1) local control, by generating target atoms and functional groups at specified positions; and (2) global control, by customizing the overall structural and physicochemical properties within defined ranges. In this way, our framework advances interpretability from post-hoc analysis to actionable generative control. Experiments show that SpaRE can generate chemically desirable molecules under complex constraints in real-world scenarios, while offering mechanistic insights for quantitative structure-property analysis. The code and demo are available at https://github.com/WanyuGroup/ICML2026_SpaRE.

title: Large Language Model Risk of Bias Assessment for Studies in Environmental Health: Proof-of-Concept Study.
desc: [JMIR bioinformatics and biotechnology] The assessment of the risk of bias (RoB) of each study is a necessary but labor-intensive step in conducting a systematic review (SR). There is a potential for AI to reduce the time and effort needed for RoB assessment and improve consistency between reviewers, but little is known about the accuracy of AI-based RoB assessments. In this study, we aim to evaluate the performance of a large language model (LLM) when given the questions from the RoB tool and the relevant passages from the full-text papers in assessing RoB in observational studies of environmental exposures and health outcomes. We evaluated the performance of GPT-5-mini on 128 observational studies from a SR of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances and health outcomes conducted by the National Academies of Sciences. The navigation guide (NavGuide), a domain-based RoB tool designed for environmental studies, was used. For each paper-domain pair, the LLM was provided with the questions and guidance from the NavGuide and the human-identified text passages addressing that domain. The LLM returned a structured RoB rating, which was compared to the human-adjudicated ratings to quantify agreement and identify patterns of discrepancy. GPT-5-mini RoB assessments for exact matches (64.5%; κ=0.199, Gwet AC2=0.882, F1-score=0.311) remained lower than the concordance between humans and the reference standard (87.5%-91.4%). Performance improved substantially for partial matches, reflecting agreement in direction but not necessarily in magnitude (eg, "low" and "probably low"), with percent concordance of 91.9% (κ=0.241, Gwet AC2=0.910, F1-score=0.614; for humans, 97.9%-98.6% concordance). Performance varied across the NavGuide domains, with the worst performance in domain 1 (selection bias) and the best in domain 4 (outcome assessment). The models tended to be more stringent than humans, often assigning higher RoB ratings (eg, "probably low" when humans assigned "low"). Our results suggest that although concordance was moderate and inconsistent across domains, LLMs may be sufficiently accurate for use with human oversight. LLMs can flag cases for human adjudication or consistency checking but are not ready for use as an independent second reviewer without human oversight.

title: PathXAI: Evidence-guided structured pathology reporting by transferable tissue segmentation
desc: Pathology reporting requires translating tissue observations across regions and slides into specific diagnoses and supporting morphological descriptions. However, the use of explicit tissue-composition measurements to guide H&E-based report generation remains underexplored. Thus, we developed PathXAI, which combines segmentation-derived tissue information with H&E images and optional domain knowledge to guide diagnostic reasoning, targeted reinspection and structured report writing. Its segmentation component exceeded baselines in mean Dice on internal and external tests. In automated report evaluation on 1,200 public and 151 private cases, PathXAI achieved higher agreement with reference diagnoses and documented morphology than the H&E-based comparators. On the public evaluation cohort, PathXAI-Report exceeded Qwen + H&E in cancer family match rate by 4.4 percentage points and in finding F1 by 5.7 percentage points. PathXAI generates evidence-linked reports with a self-hosted pretrained vision-language model, without updating its weights.

title: Beyond Model Choice: A Harness-Centered Framework for Designing Clinical Large Language Model Agents.
source: PubMed · Journal of medical Internet research
desc: [Journal of medical Internet research] Clinical large language model agents depend on both model capability and the surrounding system that selects information, constrains actions, and verifies execution. In this Viewpoint, we argue that this harness should be an explicit unit of clinical agent design, evaluation, and reporting. Our aim is to help clinical informatics and development teams specify this layer and to help evaluators and institutional governance teams assess its contributions and risks. Selected benchmarks show substantial performance differences across harness configurations, but architecture comparisons, bundled improvements, and within-model component comparisons support different levels of causal attribution. We propose a revisable 3-tier framework: tier 1 specifies general orchestration functions, including prompts, tools, output schemas, control flow, memory, and generic verification; tier 2 specifies their clinical adaptations for knowledge integration, differential reasoning, missingness and temporality, safety verification, and workflow alignment; and tier 3 specifies a failure-driven evaluation cycle applied to both. Our contribution is a framework that makes these connections explicit. We provide classification rules, an illustrative clinical example, a proposed evaluation protocol, and a minimum reporting checklist. Observable execution traces are distinguished from private model reasoning, with provenance and privacy safeguards supporting retrospective reconstruction. Evaluation should separate task success, clinical correctness, process safety, and operational reliability. Lightweight fine-tuning can complement harness design; their interaction requires controlled study. The framework is a proposal for empirical testing, not a validated taxonomy or evidence of deployment safety.

title: KnowEvo: Knowledge Evolution for Protein Optimization
desc: Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise in scientific discovery, yet systematically accumulating and refining reusable scientific knowledge remains challenging. Existing approaches primarily improve LLM-based problem solving through parameter optimization or feedback-driven refinement of prompts, programs, and solution trajectories, leaving acquired expertise either embedded in model weights or scattered across iterative problem-solving processes. As a result,knowledge is difficult to systematically inspect, evaluate, and refine. We propose KnowEvo, a framework that treats externalized knowledge itself as the optimization target. Our key insight is that scientific knowledge is inherently modular: multiple interacting mechanisms jointly determine the design outcomes. This makes knowledge evolution fundamentally challenging, as improvements cannot be attributed to individual components in isolation. To address this, KnowEvo represents knowledge as executable expertise blocks and organizes their refinements into strategy mutation trees, enabling structured exploration over a combinatorial knowledge space. The framework combines a Thompson-style forward allocation strategy that adaptively distributes evaluation budgets across strategy variants with a backward revision process, in which a code agent operates in an isolated sandbox to translate rollout evidence into localized program updates. This design enables persistent accumulation, evaluation, and refinement of mechanistic expertise across iterative experimentation. We evaluate KnowEvo on protein optimization tasks including stability and solubility. Results show that knowledge evolution consistently improves over initial strategy blocks and outperforms monolithic program evolution and prior LLM-guided evolution baselines across metrics such as pass@k, MRR, MAP,and NDCG@5. Code is available at https://github.com/recynie/KnowEvo.

title: Artificial intelligence analysis of oral mucosal lesions in white-light clinical photographs: A systematic review of visual features and validation.
source: PubMed · European journal of oral sciences
desc: [European journal of oral sciences] Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to conventional oral photographs for recognition, classification, localization, segmentation, and risk assessment of oral mucosal lesions. This systematic review evaluated how clinically relevant visual information-including color, texture, morphology, borders, and spatial patterns-is represented by AI systems and assessed performance, validation, explainability, human comparison, and clinical translation. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for studies directly analyzing conventional white-light clinical photographs. Risk of bias was assessed with PROBAST + AI, and certainty with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation-based approaches. Fifty-three studies were included, 30 published in 2025-2026. Forty-six used implicit deep-learning visual representations, three multimodal vision-language models, two explicit color analyses, and two explicit texture analyses. Thirty-one studies primarily addressed image-level diagnostic classification/recognition, 15 spatial detection/localization or lesion delineation, six screening/triage/referral or biopsy-oriented decision support, and one longitudinal malignant-transformation prediction. Six used independent external cohorts and five compared AI with human readers. Methodological concerns were frequent, no sufficiently coherent group supported meta-analysis, and certainty remained limited across evidence bodies. Current evidence therefore supports technical feasibility rather than established clinical effectiveness, with translation requiring stronger patient-level independence, external validation, prospective multicenter evaluation, and evidence of clinical benefit.

title: GRAC: Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Captioning for Surgical Scene Description
desc: Purpose: Surgical operative reports support procedural documentation, surgical training, performance assessment, and workflow review. However, extracting meaningful information often requires extensive manual review and clinical expertise. Automated surgical scene descriptions could reduce this burden by leveraging recurring surgical activities and prior knowledge. Methods: We propose GRAC (Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Captioning), a framework that represents surgical scenes as graphs capturing relationships among instruments, actions, and anatomical structures. Given an input scene graph, GRAC learns to retrieve relevant graph-caption pairs from training data. It compares instrument-tissue interactions between retrieved examples and the input scene, using comparison features to condition retrieved-caption representations during generation. Results: On the EndoVis-18 benchmark, GRAC achieved a CIDEr-D of 5.88, compared with 4.23 for SGT and 3.36 for the strongest conventional Transformer baseline. Exact instrument-action-target triplet-set accuracy reached 52.6%, compared with 32.7% for SGT and 26.2% for the strongest conventional baseline. These results demonstrate improvements in language quality and factual agreement. On TORS, GRAC achieved a CIDEr-D of 5.06, compared with 3.80 for the strongest baseline. Conclusion: GRAC demonstrates that combining structured surgical scene representations with retrieved examples improves surgical scene captioning and produces more contextually meaningful descriptions.

title: Development and Evaluation of a Transformer-Based Multi-Scale Feature Model for the Classification of Benign and Malignant Breast Lesions in Ultrasound Image.
desc: [Ultrasonic imaging] This study introduces MSF-US, a novel deep learning framework integrating multi-scale feature fusion and attention mechanisms. It aims to enhance early breast cancer detection and improve diagnostic accuracy in ultrasound images, particularly addressing the challenges of capturing global and local features in dense breast tissue. The MSF-US model combines hierarchical multi-scale feature extraction with attention mechanisms to selectively focus on diagnostically relevant regions. The framework was rigorously validated on a multi-center dataset of breast ultrasound images. Its performance was compared against state-of-the-art models, such as ResNet-50, Vision Transformer (ViT), and Swin Transformer, evaluating accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and area under the curve (AUC). In 5-fold cross-validation, MSF-US yielded an average accuracy of 0.9057, sensitivity of 0.9075, and AUC of 0.9212 with high net clinical benefit. On the independent C3 test set, it surpassed 8 SOTA baselines with a peak accuracy of 0.9406, F1 score of 0.9483, and AUC of 0.9391. Evaluation on 3 diverse public cohorts (BUSI, BUS-BRA, and BrEaST) confirmed excellent cross-center generalizability, achieving AUCs up to 0.9519. Ablation analysis validated that the synergy of multi-scale feature fusion and attention mechanisms significantly boosted diagnostic precision over single-scale baselines. MSF-US delivers state-of-the-art performance in breast ultrasound imaging, offering a highly reliable tool for early breast cancer detection. Its innovative design successfully addresses the limitations of existing methods, presenting significant clinical potential to improve diagnostic accuracy and patient outcomes.

title: Designing Effective Monitor-Based Interventions for Mitigating Reward Hacking During RL
desc: Reinforcement learning (RL) rewards are notoriously difficult to design and control, often leading to the model learning unintended behaviors such as reward hacking. One potential solution is to monitor for reward hacking and penalize it when detected; however, training against a monitor could lead to evasive behavior, and our general understanding of how to apply monitors effectively during training is limited. To study how best to use monitors to mitigate reward hacking, we introduce and open source three realistic environments where Qwen3-4B reward hacks: a coding environment hackable via test overwriting, a medical chat environment hackable via sycophancy, and a biography generation environment hackable via hallucination. We first focus on the coding environment, where we find that: (1) models can learn to evade highly accurate monitors by exploiting systemic flaws in probes and LLM judges; (2) monitors that leak more learning signal during RL suppress reward hacking but are more often evaded; and (3) including easier problems in training can decrease reward hacking. We apply our findings to build better reward hacking monitors for the medical chat and biography generation environments that improve upon naive baselines to reduce reward hacking rates across seeds to before-training levels in some interventions. Our results demonstrate that our takeaways translate to new settings and that better monitor intervention designs are possible.

title: Multimodal Machine Learning and AI-Accelerated Electrocatalytic CO2 Reduction Towards Self-Interpretable Discovery Loops.
desc: [ChemSusChem] Electrochemical CO2 reduction (CO2RR) converts renewable electricity into fuels and chemicals, but experimental chemists still struggle to track the structural evolution of CO2RR catalysts under reaction conditions and systematically optimize intertwined factors governing performance. However, interface dynamics under bias and reaction networks are complex, data are scattered across techniques and papers, and many catalyst "design rules" remain qualitative. Herein, we present machine learning (ML) as a practical data-driven toolkit for integrating information from simulations, operando characterization, microscopy, and the literature to develop quantitative descriptions of CO2RR. We first discuss how artificial intelligence (AI) accelerates time- and resource-intensive ab initio simulations, and the analysis of operando spectroscopic and electron microscopy, enabling more accurate identification of the dynamic structural and electronic evolution of catalysts under reaction conditions. Then, from a data science perspective, we review how AI enables the systematic, large-scale construction of knowledge frameworks, databases, and integrated platforms for carbon dioxide reduction. Building on these mechanistic and data foundations, we highlight ML-guided discovery loops that couple interpretable models, generative design, autonomous experimentation, and expert intervention to identify new catalysts, interfacial optimization, and operating conditions. We hope this review helps CO2RR researchers to use AI-assisted approaches to designing, understanding, and optimizing their own catalyst systems.

title: The Role Of Recurrent Refinement In Medical Image Segmentation
desc: While feed-forward segmentation networks perform well on large cohorts, they degrade in constrained clinical settings with few training samples and imaging artifacts. Human vision, by contrast, remains robust under these conditions, a property partly attributed to the recurrent and feedback connectivity of the visual cortex, which refines visual information over time. Inspired by this, we append lightweight recurrent refinement blocks to segmentation backbones, namely Conditional Random Fields (CRFs), modern Hopfield networks and convolutional GRUs, and study their behaviour as the number of iterations increases at test time (including beyond the training horizon). Evaluated on two open-source datasets, Kvasir- SEG and ARCADE, our recurrent blocks add less than 1.5% parameters and yield gains on clean data (up to 1.4 pp) and under noise (up to 17 pp) while reducing HD95. Code is available at https://github.com/joaodsmarques/recurrencehelpsegmentation .

title: Evidence of limited biases in probed language-based assessments.
source: PubMed · Journal of psychopathology and clinical science
desc: [Journal of psychopathology and clinical science] Large language models enable increasingly accurate language-based assessments (LBAs) of psychopathology. As these tools are more widely deployed in real-world settings, a critical question emerges: Do these tools work equally well for everyone? We examined whether probed LBAs, in which individuals respond to open-ended mental health questions in their own words, exhibit systematic biases that could undermine their clinical utility. We collected open-ended mental health descriptions from 1,260 participants alongside validated depression (Patient Health Questionnaire-9) and anxiety (Generalized Anxiety Disorder Scale-7) scores. We converted these descriptions to numeric representations using large-language-model-generated embeddings and applied ridge regression to predict symptom severity, achieving strong predictive accuracy (r > .60). We then examined whether assessment differences were systematically associated with sociodemographic factors (gender, age, education, employment, and income) or linguistic characteristics. Our analysis revealed limited evidence of demographic or linguistic bias: Most variables showed minimal association with assessment errors (i.e., the absolute differences between the LBAs and self-reports). However, higher depression and anxiety severity were associated with larger absolute assessment differences (standardized β = .193, p = .038; β = .252, p = .003). We explored mitigation strategies, finding that downsampling training data eliminated the bias for depression and anxiety. Our findings indicate that probed LBAs exhibit limited bias overall, particularly regarding sociodemographic equity. However, the observed severity-related pattern highlights a fundamental challenge. title: Causal graph fusion across incomplete cohorts and causal steering of tabular foundation models
desc: Clinical data are split across incomplete cohorts with partially overlapping variables. Causal discovery under missing data and multi-source integration have developed separately, and tabular foundation models cannot take a causal graph without retraining. We make two contributions. First, causal graph fusion learns a partial ancestral graph on the shared variables, fuses it into each cohort's graph under temporal background knowledge and lets Markov blankets guide re-imputation, so missing data are handled inside discovery. Second, causal attention steering compiles the learned graph into the attention of a frozen tabular foundation model at inference. Against known ground truth, fusion dominates pooled and per-cohort baselines in every missingness and heterogeneity condition tested (p<0.001), and steering improves discrimination under distribution shift (p<10^{-5}), a gain that a random graph does not produce. In two spinal cord injury cohorts, fusion orients age, albumin and hemoglobin as ancestors of length of stay, a set no single cohort orients in full, and yields compact, temporally ordered predictor sets that match or exceed automatic feature selection on four of five outcomes.

title: SeqSol-FECS: An Integrated Deep Learning and Structural Modeling Framework for Protein Solubility Engineering.
desc: [Biomacromolecules] Escherichia coli is widely used as a workhorse for heterologous protein expression. However, insoluble protein expression is frequently encountered. The mechanisms underlying protein solubility remain incompletely understood, limiting the effectiveness of current protein solubility engineering strategies. Here, SeqSol, a sequence-level solubility prediction model capable of prioritizing single-amino-acid substitutions through WT-mutant rescoring, was developed using 71,425 proteins. SeqSol achieved an accuracy of 75.8% and an AUC of 0.840 on an independent test set and correctly identified experimentally validated solubility-enhancing mutations from diverse proteins. To minimize the risk of activity loss, candidate mutation sites were prioritized according to conformational flexibility, relative solvent accessibility, and evolutionary conservation before solubility engineering. Using only 30 experimentally tested mutations, the resulting SeqSol-FECS framework increased the solubility of two industrial enzymes from 56.18% and 10.53% to over 95%, respectively, while maintaining their specific activities. SeqSol-FECS provides an efficient strategy for enzyme solubility engineering and biomanufacturing applications.

title: Forecasting cumulative intraoperative hypotension burden: patient-disjoint evaluation of quantile boosting and alert policies
desc: Background: Binary hypotension forecasts do not describe the depth and duration of future low pressure. Burden forecasts may support graded early warning, but better forecast scores need not yield more useful alerts. Objective: To evaluate conditional quantiles of the next 15-minute mean arterial pressure (MAP) deficit below 65 mmHg and distinguish forecasting performance from episode-warning performance. Methods: Public VitalDB numeric arterial MAP was reduced to 10-second medians without forward filling. Subject-disjoint training, validation and test splits included 70,402, 14,270 and 15,575 labeled windows. We compared climatology, calibrated persistence, last-MAP-only boosting, and direct and residual quantile boosting, with and without additional MAP-history features. Patient-weighted pinball loss and subject-bootstrap intervals evaluated forecasting. Validation selected alert thresholds before a hash-recorded test evaluation. Results: In the test split, the prespecified residual-versus-persistence comparison at the 90th percentile yielded losses of 2.256 and 2.900 mmHg-min, respectively (difference -0.644; 95% interval -0.814 to -0.487). Direct prediction achieved 2.196, and direct prediction with additional MAP features achieved 2.193. Episode-warning results were sensitive to the alert rule and operating threshold. Conclusions: This retrospective benchmark separates burden-forecast skill from warning-policy performance. Findings support further study of direct burden estimation; they do not establish patient benefit, prospective reliability or transportability beyond the source hospital.

title: Deep learning-based myocardial segmentation using non-contrast-enhanced CT for quantitative SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging.
desc: [EJNMMI physics] Accurate myocardial segmentation is essential for polar map-based quantitative analysis in SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI). Commercial software requires significant manual adjustment to ensure accurate segmentation, particularly for studies with severe myocardial defects or high extracardiac uptake. To address this limitation, we propose deep learning (DL)-based myocardial segmentation using non-contrast-enhanced CT images. Myocardial masks were generated by simply thresholding PET images with uniform myocardial uptake in 125 18F-FDG PET/CT studies. An optimal network was configured through the nn-UNet pipeline with CT images as input and the masks as labels. For evaluation, the network was tested on 50 99mTc-sestamibi SPECT/CT MPI studies with uniform myocardial uptake. Additional 50 SPECT MPI studies with severe myocardial defects or high extracardiac uptake were selected to demonstrate the impact of using DL-masks on polar map-based quantification. Three nuclear cardiologists visually compared myocardium contours with and without DL-masks in commercial software. DL-masks achieved a Dice Similarity Coefficient of 0.866 ± 0.035 in the PET/CT validation set and 0.846 ± 0.026 in the SPECT/CT test set. For additional studies, segmental differences in the polar map with and without DL-masks indicated meaningful quantitative differences (~ 10%) in basal segments near the septum, compared to mid-cavity or apical segments. Likert scoring demonstrated that DL-masks improved septal and valve plane placement in commercial software, resulting in accurate myocardial segmentation without manual adjustment. We demonstrated a DL segmentation model for accurate myocardial segmentation without manual adjustment and corresponding polar map-based quantification, particularly in studies with severe myocardial defects or high extracardiac uptake.

title: Finite-sample Calibration Guarantees for Binary Segmentation
desc: Machine learning based segmentation models are frequently miscalibrated, producing for each pixel a label prediction whose associated confidence does not accurately reflect the true underlying probability. This limitation is particularly critical in high-stakes applications such as medical image segmentation. Although several calibration methods have been proposed, only a small subset of them provides theoretical guarantees on the calibration error, i.e., they do not typically ensure that, with high probability, the model exhibits a low calibration error. In this work, we develop a post-hoc calibration method for which formal calibration guarantees can be established. To achieve this, we derive from standard concentration inequalities an improved theoretical bound that explicitly accounts for the spatial dependence inherent in binary segmentation outputs. We empirically demonstrate that the proposed calibrator satisfies the derived guarantee and outperforms existing post-hoc calibration approaches.

title: A mixed methods evaluation of confidence, competence, and perceived value following a Teaching Institute on artificial intelligence for gerontology educators.
desc: [Gerontology & geriatrics education] As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly embedded in higher education, gerontology educators face new opportunities and ethical challenges when integrating AI tools into teaching, mentorship, and professional practice. Rapid advances in AI, alongside evolving aging research and policy, require educators to adapt their pedagogical approaches. Organizers for the Academy for Gerontology in Higher Education's 14th Annual Teaching Institute sought to address this need by providing instructor-focused professional development on emerging issues of AI in gerontology education, with an emphasis on ethical, inclusive, and discipline-specific applications. In this paper, we describe the rationale, structure, and content of the 14th Annual Teaching Institute and examine its impact on instructor confidence and perceived competence with utilizing AI professionally. A mixed methods evaluation of the workshop included pre- and post-surveys, confidence ratings, and qualitative feedback from attendees (N = 21). Quantitative results demonstrated statistically significant increases in confidence and perceived competence using AI across multiple professional domains. Qualitative findings highlighted the value of peer learning, hands-on activities, and contextualized discussions of AI in gerontology education. Findings suggest that structured, interactive professional development can enhance instructors' capacity to engage critically and responsibly with AI while reinforcing core gerontology competencies.

title: RuACT: Recovering Inactive Rubrics as Adaptive Critics and Teachers
desc: Rubric-based reinforcement learning (RL) extends RL with verifiable rewards to open-ended tasks by scoring each response against query-specific rubrics. Under group-relative optimization, however, a rubric that every sampled response fails (unreachable) or passes (saturated) gives all responses the same outcome and no learning signal; in Qwen3-4B medical training, 60.88% of query-rubric observations are inactive. We find that the two states lack different supervision: stating an unreachable rubric in the prompt raises its satisfaction from 1.13% to 91.25%, whereas responses that all pass a saturated rubric still differ in quality. We therefore propose RuACT (Rubrics as Adaptive Critics and Teachers), which assigns each inactive rubric the role that supplies what it lacks. Rubric as Teacher uses unreachable rubrics as privileged information for reward-gated on-policy self-distillation, and Rubric as Critic decomposes saturated rubrics into child rubrics that separate current responses while sharing the parent's weight. RuACT outperforms GRPO, rubric reweighting, and rubric-guided exploration on all four medical and scientific benchmarks with Qwen3-4B and achieves the best average with Qwen3-1.7B. On initially unreachable rubrics, unguided recovery rises from 35.02% to 42.86%, while child refinement improves reward-quality alignment on independent rollouts from 57.74% to 60.77%. Code is available at https://github.com/ZJU-REAL/RuACT.

title: Impact of training data on deep learning-based RNA 3D structure quality assessment.
desc: [Briefings in bioinformatics] Accurate reference-free assessment of predicted RNA 3D structures is essential for large-scale RNA modeling, yet the impact of training data on deep learning-based quality predictors remains poorly understood. Here, we present a systematic cross-training analysis of three deep learning predictors for RNA 3D structure quality assessment, each originally developed on distinct training sets. By retraining each predictor on alternative (nonnative) datasets-including RNA3DQA, a new set created specifically for this project-and evaluating performance on independent RNA-Puzzles benchmarks, we systematically assess the relative contributions of model architecture and training data composition. Our results reveal pronounced differences in cross-dataset generalization, with predictors often performing better when trained on nonnative datasets than on their native ones. Notably, the impact of the training datasets varied across predictors, with RNA3DQA yielding the overall best accuracy and ranking stability results specifically for the ARES model. Native training sets yielded better performance for RNA3DCNN and lociPARSE. These findings demonstrate that the characteristics of the training data play a dominant, model-dependent role in shaping the performance and robustness of reference-free RNA 3D structure quality assessment methods. We conclude with practical recommendations for designing transferable training datasets and for benchmarking deep learning-based quality predictors in RNA structural bioinformatics.

title: Mosaic:montage-agnostic self-distilled graph learning for subject-independent ieeg seizure detection
desc: Intracranial EEG provides high signal-to-noise ratio and spatial resolution for detecting epileptic activity, but patient-specific electrode placement leads to substantial variation in channel count and montage across subjects. This heterogeneity limits the generalization of existing detectors under subject-independent evaluation. We propose MOSAIC (MOntage-agnostic Self-distilled Adaptive Inter-channel Connectivity learning), a lightweight graph-learning framework for subject-independent iEEG seizure detection. MOSAIC pairs a shared convolutional channel encoder with a patient-agnostic channel-attention module that infers a weighted inter-channel adjacency matrix from the encoded features, requiring no fixed montage graph. An exponential moving average self-distillation objective regularizes each prediction toward a slowly updated per-patient teacher. Across four public iEEG corpora (SWEC-ETHZ long- and short-term, Mayo, FNUSA), MOSAIC outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in F2 and Cohen's $κ$ while learning more stable inter-channel adjacencies, demonstrating that self-distilled connectivity learning transfers across unseen implantations.

title: Deep-Learning-Empowered Gold Nanoparticle Dimer-Assisted Hyperbolic Metamaterial Surface Plasmon Resonance Fiber-Optic Sensor for Ultrasensitive Mercury Ion Detection.
desc: [ACS applied materials & interfaces] Mercury ions (Hg2+) are highly toxic heavy-metal contaminants that pose serious environmental and health hazards, necessitating the development of highly sensitive and accurate detection methods. Herein, a fiber-optic surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensor is developed for the ultrasensitive detection of Hg2+. The sensing probe is constructed on a hyperbolic metamaterial (HMM) consisting of three repeated Ag/ITO bilayers, decorated with thymine (T)-rich DNA-functionalized gold nanoparticles (AuNPs). Upon Hg2+ addition, specific T-Hg2+-T coordination captures a second population of DNA-functionalized AuNPs, forming AuNP dimers on the HMM surface. The nanometer interparticle gap of the AuNP dimer induces strong plasmonic coupling, which amplifies the local refractive index (RI) changes at the sensing interface and produces a pronounced SPR wavelength shift, enabling highly sensitive detection of Hg2+. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed sensor exhibits a peak RI sensitivity of 8600 nm/RIU and achieves a limit of detection as low as 2.63 pM for Hg2+. Moreover, a DenseNet-based deep-learning model is employed to extract subtle spectral features from SPR spectra acquired at seven Hg2+ concentration levels, enabling quantitative concentration prediction with an R2 of 0.998505. Therefore, the proposed fiber-optic SPR sensor provides a promising strategy for sensitive and accurate Hg2+ detection.

title: Optimal scenario design for climate emulation.
source: PubMed · Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
desc: [Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America] As deep learning for physical systems continues to grow in popularity, efforts to improve generalizability have primarily focused on designing architectures that embed physical constraints. However, for machine-learning surrogate climate models (emulators), we show that the low structural diversity in existing scenarios commonly used to generate training data places a ceiling on predictive skill. Here, we examine whether training datasets themselves can be optimized to improve generalization. We introduce a method to create datasets that produce emulators capable of generalizing to new, structurally different scenarios absent from the training data. We use a differentiable simple climate model (SCM) to calculate the sensitivity of emulator loss to perturbations in the training data, iteratively updating the training data to maximize emulator skill. For an SCM, an emulator trained on one scenario optimized in this fashion outperforms an emulator trained on six standard Scenario Model Intercomparison Project (ScenarioMIP) pathways. We achieve this higher predictive skill despite training on a smaller dataset, finding that our emulator successfully isolates distinct physical behaviors of different climate forcing agents (e.g., greenhouse gases vs. aerosols) without single-forcing runs. We then demonstrate that scenarios optimized using an SCM, when used to drive an intermediate-complexity climate model, produce a training dataset that yields a more skillful emulator than training on ScenarioMIP outputs. Our results suggest that, in the compute-constrained environment of running full-scale climate models, generating a small number of dynamically rich scenarios provides greater marginal value for emulation and characterizing system responses than expanding the suite of traditional emissions pathways.

title: Artificial Intelligence Use in Interventional Clinical Trials Registered on ClinicalTrials.gov.
desc: [JAMA network open]
